ingredients.name: Vitamin B12
ingredients.absorption: synthetic; ~1-2% passive at 1000 mcg, requires conversion to methyl/adenosyl forms
ingredients.notes: Cyanocobalamin is the most clinically studied and commonly used supplemental B12 form. It is converted to active cobalamin forms after absorption. At equivalent supplemental doses, reviewed evidence does not establish inferior clinical efficacy or absorption versus other oral B12 forms. Evidence: NIH ODS Vitamin B12 fact sheet; PMID:18709891.

condition_hits.mechanism: Observational associations between B12 status and recurrent pregnancy loss do not establish a universal optimal level above 400 pg/mL or prove improved pregnancy outcomes from targeting it.
condition_hits.action: Discuss B12 testing or supplementation with your clinician if deficiency is suspected. Treat documented deficiency using clinical guidance rather than a registry-specific target above 400 pg/mL.
condition_hits.alert_body: Vitamin B12 used while trying to conceive is often continued through pregnancy as part of prenatal care. If you are planning pregnancy, discuss dosing of Vitamin B12 with your clinician.
condition_hits.informational_note: Vitamin B12 is continued under clinician guidance — relevant to people planning pregnancy.

condition_hits.mechanism: B12 is essential throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding, and supplementation started pre-conception should continue. If you are pregnant or nursing, discuss dosing with your obstetrician.
condition_hits.alert_body: B12 is essential throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding, and supplementation started pre-conception should continue. If you are pregnant or nursing, discuss dosing with your obstetrician.

condition_hits.alert_body: B12 is essential throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding, and supplementation started pre-conception should continue. If you are pregnant or nursing, discuss dosing with your obstetrician.

pregnancy_lactation.mechanism: B12 is an essential nutrient throughout pregnancy and lactation. Deficiency is associated with neural tube defects, developmental delay, and recurrent pregnancy loss via hyperhomocysteinemia. Standard prenatal vitamins contain B12; supplementation should continue throughout pregnancy and during breastfeeding.
pregnancy_lactation.notes: B12 supplementation during pregnancy is part of standard prenatal care. Vegans and those with malabsorption (pernicious anemia, gastric surgery, metformin use) need higher supplemental doses.
pregnancy_lactation.alert_body: B12 is essential throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding, and supplementation started pre-conception should continue. If you are pregnant or nursing, discuss dosing with your obstetrician.
pregnancy_lactation.informational_note: B12 is part of standard prenatal support — relevant to anyone pregnant or breastfeeding.

ingredients.name: Cannabidiol

condition_hits.mechanism: Prescription cannabidiol can cause dose-related liver-enzyme elevations, with greater risk in some patients taking valproate or with elevated baseline enzymes. Hepatic impairment can also increase cannabidiol exposure. The EPIDIOLEX warning concerns its tested prescription formulation.
condition_hits.action: Use CBD only with clinician guidance if you have liver disease. Prescription EPIDIOLEX requires liver monitoring; its label directs discontinuation for transaminases above 3 times ULN together with bilirubin above 2 times ULN, or sustained transaminases above 5 times ULN. The prescribing clinician should manage treatment changes.
condition_hits.alert_body: CBD is processed by the liver and can raise liver enzymes, especially at higher doses or with other liver-metabolized medicines. If you have liver disease, use only with clinician guidance.
condition_hits.informational_note: CBD is liver-metabolized — relevant to people with liver conditions.

condition_hits.mechanism: CBD has anticonvulsant properties (FDA-approved for Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes). However, CBD supplements are not pharmaceutical-grade and have variable potency, contaminant profiles, and dosing. Interaction with existing anticonvulsant regimens (especially valproate) may cause hepatotoxicity or alter drug levels.
condition_hits.action: Use only pharmaceutical-grade CBD (Epidiolex) for seizure management. Supplement-grade CBD should not be substituted. Inform neurologist of any CBD use.
condition_hits.alert_body: Prescription cannabidiol treats specific seizure disorders, but OTC CBD products vary in dose and purity. If you have seizures or take antiseizure medication, use CBD only with clinician guidance.
condition_hits.informational_note: CBD may affect seizure threshold — relevant to people with a seizure disorder.

condition_hits.mechanism: FDA strongly advises against CBD use during pregnancy. Animal studies show potential risks to the developing fetus. No adequate human safety data exists for CBD during pregnancy.
condition_hits.action: Avoid CBD supplements during pregnancy. Consult healthcare provider.
condition_hits.alert_headline: FDA advises against use in pregnancy
condition_hits.alert_body: FDA strongly advises against CBD use in pregnancy based on animal studies. If you are pregnant, talk to your obstetrician before any CBD product.
condition_hits.informational_note: CBD lacks pregnancy safety data — relevant to anyone pregnant or planning pregnancy.

condition_hits.mechanism: FDA strongly advises against CBD during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Avoid CBD products and discuss any exposure with your clinician.
condition_hits.alert_body: FDA strongly advises against CBD during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Avoid CBD products and discuss any exposure with your clinician.

drug_class_hits.mechanism: The EPIDIOLEX label reports increased exposure to N-desmethylclobazam during concomitant clobazam use and a higher liver-enzyme elevation risk with valproate. These findings apply to the studied prescription cannabidiol preparation and specific combinations; the label does not establish identical effects for every anticonvulsant.
drug_class_hits.action: Ask your neurologist before adding CBD. The prescriber should manage clobazam-related adverse effects, liver monitoring with valproate, and any medication adjustment.
drug_class_hits.alert_body: CBD can influence how seizure medications work. If you take an anticonvulsant, talk to your neurologist before adding CBD.
drug_class_hits.informational_note: CBD may affect anticonvulsant therapy — relevant to people on seizure medications.

drug_class_hits.mechanism: The EPIDIOLEX label advises monitoring and possible dose adjustment for susceptible oral P-glycoprotein substrates, including tacrolimus and sirolimus. This should not be generalized to clinically proven inhibition of all CYP3A4 substrates.
drug_class_hits.action: Monitor tacrolimus/sirolimus trough levels closely. Dose reduction for the immunosuppressant should be considered. Inform transplant team of CBD use.
drug_class_hits.alert_headline: May increase exposure to some transplant drugs
drug_class_hits.alert_body: CBD can increase exposure to certain transplant drugs. Talk to your transplant prescriber before use; appropriate drug-level monitoring or prescribed dose adjustment may be needed.
drug_class_hits.informational_note: CBD affects immune function — relevant to people on immunosuppressants.

drug_class_hits.mechanism: Case reports describe INR increases during cannabinoid use with warfarin. Evidence quality is low, and this does not establish a uniform anticoagulant-class effect or direct antiplatelet activity.
drug_class_hits.action: Monitor INR more frequently when starting or stopping CBD. Inform prescriber.
drug_class_hits.alert_body: Case reports link cannabinoid use to INR changes with warfarin. Tell your anticoagulant prescriber about CBD use; warfarin users may need closer INR checks when use changes.
drug_class_hits.informational_note: CBD can affect clotting — relevant to people on anticoagulants.

drug_class_hits.mechanism: CBD has CNS depressant effects and may potentiate sedation when combined with benzodiazepines, opioids, or other sedatives.
drug_class_hits.action: Use caution with concurrent sedative medications. Monitor for excessive drowsiness.
drug_class_hits.alert_body: CBD has mild sedative effects. If you take a sedative or sleep medication, talk to your prescriber before adding CBD — the combination can increase drowsiness.
drug_class_hits.informational_note: CBD has sedative activity — relevant to people on sedatives or sleep medications.

pregnancy_lactation.notes: FDA strongly advises against CBD during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Animal studies show developmental toxicity. CBD transfers to breast milk.
pregnancy_lactation.alert_headline: Avoid CBD during pregnancy and breastfeeding
pregnancy_lactation.alert_body: FDA strongly advises against CBD during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Avoid CBD products and discuss any exposure with your clinician.
pregnancy_lactation.informational_note: CBD lacks pregnancy safety data — relevant to anyone pregnant or planning pregnancy.

verified_sources.title: FDA Regulation of Cannabis and Cannabis-Derived Products, Including CBD
verified_sources.evidence_summary: FDA states THC/CBD products are excluded from dietary supplement definition under FD&C Act section 201(ff)(3)(B). Q&A9 distinguishes cannabis-derived ingredients without THC or CBD from the excluded THC/CBD substances; hemp or phytocannabinoid wording alone does not identify CBD.
